test_title: SSC CPO 2022 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On 11 Nov 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Hold your horses

options.text: To keep the horse chain intact
Holding and keeping things by yourself
Give time to others for some rest
To tell someone to stop and consider carefully

solution:
The correct answer is **To tell someone to stop and consider carefully**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **most appropriate** meaning for the given idiom '**Hold your horses**' is '**To tell someone to stop and consider carefully**'.
 
• **Hold your horses**: *used to tell someone to stop and consider carefully their decision or opinion about something*.
 
 
• **E.g.** *Just hold your horses, Bill! Let's think about this for a moment.**​*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at some similar idioms.
 
 
• **Cool your jets**: After the defendant's outburst in court, the judge said he could “**cool his jets**” in jail before appearing again next month.
 
• **To let your hair down**: Should we go out and **let our hair down** for a few hours at a karaoke bar?
 
• **To switch off**: My weekend was amazing. I just **switched off **completely on Friday evening, got away from everything, and didn’t pick up my mobile phone.
